questions.question_text: Atrophy of the head of caudate nucleus. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Tis is a progressive, inherited neurodegenerative disease that is characterized by autosomal dominant transmission and the emergence of abnormal involuntary movements and cognitive deterioration, with progression to dementia and death over 10–20 years.

questions.question_text: Hockey-stick sign. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Te hockey stick sign refers to bilateral symmetrical regions of hyperintensity in the pulvinar and the dorsomedial nuclei of the thalami.

questions.question_text: Hyperintensities in bilateral mammillary bodies. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Tis condition is caused by severe defciency of thiamine (Vitamin B1), which is usually caused by alcohol abuse in the Western countries. Post-mortem examination of the brains of those dying of Wernicke's encephalopathy reveals petechial haemorrhages in the mammillary bodies, walls of the third ventricle (less common than in the mammillary bodies) and periaqueductal grey matter, as well as the foor of the fourth ventricle and inferior colliculi.

questions.question_text: Pulvinar sign. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Microscopy of brain material reveals vacuolar changes in grey matter, particularly in cerebral and cerebellar cortex, creating characteristic spongiform appearances.

questions.question_text: A lesion of this particular area can lead to motor aphasia.
questions.explanation: Broca's area is the core of the frontal operculum on the dominant (usually lef) side and consists mainly of areas 44 and 45. A lesion involving this area would lead to expressive (motor) aphasia.

questions.question_text: A lesion of this area would lead to sociopathy.
questions.explanation: Lesions of the orbital cortex on either side could lead to a form of acquired sociopathy.

questions.question_text: A lesion of this area would lead to akinetic mutism.
questions.explanation: A lesion of the lef or right superior mesial region can lead to akinetic mutism.

questions.question_text: An injury to this area of the central nervous system would lead to both anterograde and retrograde amnesia.
questions.explanation: Lesions of the basal forebrain (either side) could lead to amnesia and confabulation.

questions.question_text: Which of the aforementioned is the most common cerebral tumour?
questions.explanation: Glioma is the most common tumour. It is derived from the glial cells and their precursors and includes astrocytomas, oligodendrocytomas and ependymomas.

questions.question_text: Null cell adenoma is the third most common type of which of the aforementioned.
questions.explanation: Null cell adenoma is one of the types of pituitary adenomas. Te most common variant is the sparsely granulated PRL cell adenoma.

questions.question_text: Tese tumours are derived from blood vessels.
questions.explanation: Tese are derived from blood vessels.

questions.question_text: Tese are considered to be embryonal tumours.
questions.explanation: Tese are cerebellar tumours which are embryonal in nature.

questions.question_text: In this particular form of group therapy, there is no particular end date of the therapy.
questions.explanation: In continuous group therapy, there is no defnite end date of the group therapy. Te therapy may last for years. Old members would leave, and new members could join.

questions.question_text: In this form of group therapy, replacement of group members is allowed.
questions.explanation: In open-group therapy, replacement of group members is allowed for. Tis is in contrast to closed-group therapy, in which no replacement of group members is allowed for.

questions.question_text: Tis particular form of group therapy allows the mixture of clients from difering backgrounds.
questions.explanation: Heterogeneous group therapy allows for a mixture of clients with diferent backgrounds and conditions. Tis is in contrast to homogenous group therapy, in which only members of the same gender, similar background and same conditions are included into the group.

questions.question_text: Tis helps to summarize the results of a trial and also in individualized decision making.
questions.explanation: Te number needed to treat expresses the beneft for an active treatment over a placebo. It could be used in summarizing the results of a trial and in individualized medical decision making. It takes the value of nearest integer (or whole number) equal to or higher than.

questions.question_text: Tis is a ratio of the subjects in the disease group who have been exposed to the subjects in the control group who have not been exposed.
questions.explanation: Te odds ratio is the ratio of the odds that subjects in the disease group were exposed to the factor to the odds that subjects in the control group were exposed to the factor.

questions.question_text: Tis refers to a measure of the diference in the risk between the two groups being studied but this time indexing the risk reduction following exposure to the index factor.
questions.explanation: Tis is the incidence of the disease in the group exposed to the risk factor of interest minus the incidence in the group not exposed to the risk factor.

questions.question_text: Tis is also known as the risk diference or the absolute excess risk.
questions.explanation: Te explanation is as per the preceding question.

questions.question_text: Tis refers to the ratio of the incidence of the disease in people who are exposed to the risk factor to the incidence of the disease in people who are not exposed to the same risk factor.
questions.explanation: Similarly in a cohort study, the relative risk is then the ratio of the probability of a positive outcome in the cohort group (exposed) to the probability of a positive outcome in the control group (not exposed).

questions.question_text: In depressive disorder, the concentrations of these two neuropeptides are increased in the cerebrospinal fuid.
questions.explanation: CRF concentration is increased in the CSF of depressed patients. Afer antidepressant treatment, there is a reduction in the CRF levels. It is also important to note that 25%–30% of euthyroid depressives have blunted TSH response to TRH challenge or abnormal T3/T4 levels.

questions.question_text: Overactivity of this neuropeptide leads to excessive noradrenaline release.
questions.explanation: CRH overactivity provokes the excessive release of NA in panic attacks as well as in alcohol withdrawal.

questions.question_text: Te amount of this neuropeptide is reduced in Alzheimer's disease.
questions.explanation: Tis neuropeptide has an inhibitory efect on growth hormone release. It is reduced in Alzheimer's disease and the CSF concentration is also reduced in unipolar and bipolar depression.

questions.question_text: Tis particular neuropeptide is involved in appetite and feeding, as well as in emotional behaviour.
questions.explanation: CCK regulates the postprandial release of bile locally in the gut and controls the appetite in the CNS. It is involved in appetite and feeding as well as in the modulation of emotional behaviour.

questions.question_text: Tis is a neuropeptide that inhibits the release of somatostatin.
questions.explanation: Te aforementioned is true with regards to VIP. It is found in the cerebral cortex, hypothalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, autonomic ganglia, and intestinal and respiratory tracts.

questions.question_text: Hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis is the characteristic feature of this condition.
questions.explanation: Both neuropathological and structural neuroimaging studies have indicated that hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis as well as hypoplasia of the cerebellar hemispheres occurs in individuals diagnosed with autism.

questions.question_text: In this condition, there is characteristic neuronal loss, as well as reactive astrocytosis and presence of Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra.
questions.explanation: Te histological changes in idiopathic Parkinson's disease include neuronal loss, reactive astrocytosis and the presence of Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra.

questions.question_text: In this condition, there is the dilatation of the lateral and the third ventricles, along with marked atrophy of the cerebral cortex.
questions.explanation: In this condition, the typical changes are a small brain with reduced mass, along with marked atrophy of the corpus striatum and particularly that of the caudate nucleus. Tere is the associated dilatation of the lateral and the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Buspirone exerts its clinical efects through the partial agonism of which of the aforementioned receptors?
questions.explanation: Buspirone exerts anxiolytic and antidepressant efects through the partial agonism of the 5-HT1A receptor. Aripiprazole is a 5-HT1A agonist.

questions.question_text: Tis particular receptor type is implicated in Cloninger's type II alcoholism.
questions.explanation: It is an autoreceptor which is coupled with a G protein that inhibits the intracellular messenger. It reduces the 5-HT release and is implicated in Type II alcoholism.

questions.question_text: Tis receptor is involved in the contraction of the colon and bladder.
questions.explanation: It is found in the brain stem, the substantia nigra, hippocampus as well as the frontal cortex. It is also present in the heart. Te receptor does mediate cortisol secretion and contraction of the colon and the bladder.

questions.question_text: Antagonism of this receptor helps to improve cognition.
questions.explanation: 5-HT6 is present in high levels in the olfactory tubercle, corpus striatum, the nucleus accumbens and hippocampus as well as in the cerebellum and the hippocampus. Te receptor helps to regulate the release of neurotrophic factors. Antagonism may enhance the cognition.

questions.question_text: Tis particular receptor is involved in the circadian rhythm.
questions.explanation: 5-HT7 is predominant in the thalamus and it is involved in the circadian rhythm.
